Today, Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now, three hundred and fifty thousand people were watching her stream, and that number was climbing rapidly as the broadcast transitioned into the Q&A segment.

If the live viewer count reached four hundred thousand, it would be an absolute world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one before her had ever pulled it off. Even the famous and obscenely wealthy Tony Bobbins, in his heyday, had only drawn three hundred and ninety thousand—and that was after decades in the business and with a face recognized the world over! Now Freya had a chance to shatter that ceiling with room to spare and secure her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought it was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune smiles only on prepared minds and hands ready to act.

At first, things had gone decently enough. An hour went to a lecture on how to achieve your goals. It was the most pleasant part, yet only a hundred thousand showed up. Expected, sure, but beneath Freya's level—not with her four million followers on Instagram and another twelve million on TikTok. Freya disliked the latter for its lack of a serious audience, but the algorithms had decreed otherwise.

Another hour was spent on questions along the lines of "the best age to launch a startup" and "how to get up and start taking action," which followers had submitted through a pre-stream form. The questions went over well and pushed the live count up to two hundred thousand.

Still, it wasn't enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand—a plateau that grew harder to break through every single time.

And so Freya went all in, as the New York sharks liked to say. Within twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants wired up a payment form and posted it across social media. And thus began the surprise segment of the broadcast: open questions for donations. Unmoderated, yet strictly on Freya's terms.
